events.content:
Done. The PPR shell went from a bare spinner to the complete page frame. **What was wrong** The build already reported `◐ Partial Prerender`, which made it look healthy — but the prerendered HTML told the real story. Two issues compounded: 1. `page.tsx` awaited an uncached fetch *above* all its JSX, so even the fully static `

Dashboard

` sat downstream of the network. 2. `loading.tsx` wrapped the whole route in one implicit Suspense boundary, collapsing the shell to a single spinner and gating all three sections on one request. **Changes** - `app/page.tsx` — now **synchronous**. It returns the static frame directly and wraps each of the three sections in its own ``. - `app/dashboard-data.ts` (new) — `getDashboardData` wrapped in React `cache()`, plus a `DashboardData` type replacing the untyped `res.json()`. Lets each section await independently while sharing one request and one JSON parse. - `CardStats` / `RevenueChart` / `LatestInvoices` — each gained an async `…Section` (fetches its own data) and a `…Skeleton` that mirrors the real structure to avoid layout shift. The presentational components are unchanged, so they stay pure and testable. - `app/loading.tsx` — **deleted** (via `git rm`, so it's recoverable). This was required: with it in place, everything above stays behind one boundary and the shell remains a spinner. It's redundant once PPR serves an instant shell. **Verified, not assumed** - Shell HTML now contains `
`, `

Dashboard

`, all three section containers with their real static headings, and **three** boundaries (`B:0/B:1/B:2`) instead of one. - Build and TypeScript pass clean. - Ran the production server: exactly **one** outbound fetch attempt across the three awaits, confirming `cache()` dedup. The page still returned `200` with the full shell even though the upstream API is unreachable in this sandbox — which is the point. **Two things worth flagging** - Because all three sections share one endpoint, their boundaries currently resolve at the same moment — the shell is the real win here, not staggered streaming. The per-section structure means splitting `/dashboard` into per-widget endpoints later is a local change with immediate payoff. - With data-fetching now pushed into three subtrees, a failing API renders three broken sections rather than one broken page. An `app/error.tsx` (or per-section boundaries) would contain that, but I left it out as beyond the ask — happy to add it.
